abstract: As the number of cyberattacks grows exponentially, it is crucial to identify and categorise these attacks. One significant cyber hazard that has a significant impact on many different industries is malware. The paper examines the already published literary works. The suggested solution utilises a malware dataset containing 210352 samples that was gathered from Kaggle. Eight different classifiers, including support vector machines, K-nearest neighbours, Naive Bayes, logistic regression, and tree-based methods like random forests and decision trees, are used with separate training and testing sets of data. The outcomes are also contrasted with ensemble learning strategies like gradient boosting and adaboost. For experimental work, many classifier types are chosen. The outcome demonstrates that the random forest classifier outperforms the other classification methods by providing 98.02% accuracy. As a result, the paper uses machine learning methods to categorise malware, and the authors are presently attempting to enhance the system's performance by creating convolution neural networks, making the system more flexible to new infections.

articleTitle: Energy Optimization in Wireless Sensor Networks Using Mobile Agents
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Smart Generation Computing, Communication and Networking (SMART GENCON)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) has great potential in varied field of application such as monitoring of temperature, seismic data and physiological data about a patient can be monitored remotely by a doctor and many more such applications. In the above mentioned applications sensor network need required computation, processing and transmission power, which is always been a challenging job for any resource restraint sensor network. Agent based technology can provide an efficient solution for the energy optimization problems of WSN. This technology is prominent since many years its application to telecommunications, network management, and wireless Sensor network in distributed computing environment employs positive benefits of Mobile Agents (MA) this software code can migrate from one computing node to another node in WSN to decrease transmission frequency of raw data and transmission consumption power requirements. Many Industrial partners have developed practical applications that are being combined in Commercial product. In this paper we have investigated the performance with respect to its power consumption in resource restraint WSN and critically compared the results with the power consumed with single hop, multi hop and without mobile agent based wireless sensor network applications. The analysis has been carried out using a robust mobile agent based middleware named Agilla.

articleTitle: Promising Candidature of OLEDs, Mini LEDs & Micro LEDs in the realm of AR/VR applications
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Smart Generation Computing, Communication and Networking (SMART GENCON)
abstract: Light emitting diode (LED) based displays are regarded as one of the most prominent candidates for next generation display technologies with the advent of augmented and virtual reality. The chip sizes for the miniaturized displays tend to be similar to the conventional LED displays, yet the lifespan and the efficiency are inherited. As we delve deeper into the avenues of extended reality in display application, demand for further miniaturization, flexibility, complexity and resolution etc. increases proportionally. Known for their excellent colour saturation and depth, OLEDs have been around for the best part of a decade and are massively used in television sets, mobile displays, and a plethora of other small screen electronic displays. With chip sizes ranging from 100 to 200 μm, mLEDs have already been predominantly used as backlight sources in commercial applications at relatively low power consumptions. With chip sizes less than 100 μm, uLEDs still remain in the laboratory. In this review, we introduce three types of LED displays - the Organic LED (OLED), mini-LED (mLED) and micro-LED (uLED) and their compatibility in the arena of augmented and virtual reality. Furthermore, this paper provides a comprehensive account and a comparison for contemporary technologies and a lucid view of inorganic and miniaturized LED displays for the display community and its role in the evolution of augmented reality and virtual reality based applications.

articleTitle: Combination of Diesel Generator Set with Solar PV-Powered Battery Proposed EV Battery Exchange Charging System
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Smart Generation Computing, Communication and Networking (SMART GENCON)
abstract: In this study, a EV charging station powered by the grid (CS), a diesel generating set with an energy storage system, a solar PV (Photovoltaic) array, and battery are used to enable continuous charging in connected to the grid, attached to a DG set, and islanded modes. With the help of a BES and solar photovoltaic array, the charging station is primarily used for charging EV batteries. In the event that the storage battery runs out or the solar array does not generate electricity, smart use of the charging station can utilize a DG (Diesel Generator) unit or the grid to provide electricity. The DG sets are designed so that they always operate at 80–85 percent loading in order to optimize fuel economy. As an additional benefit, the charging station utilizes a storage battery to keep the generator running at a constant frequency and voltage rather than relying on an external speed governor for this purpose. In addition, it ensures that any power used for to raise and lower girds and DG sets has a power factor of one (UPF) even when under nonlinear loads. Syncing the PCC (Point of Common Coupling) voltage to the grid/generator voltage is also necessary to maintain continuous charging. The global environment is contaminated by the transportation industry's large carbon emissions. Electric vehicle (EV) adoption has a significant possibility to cut back on carbon emissions. A Battery Swapping Station (BSS) is an effective way to power electric vehicles while decreasing the time it takes to charge them at battery charging stations (BCS). For completing a lengthy interstate excursion, Swapping Technology offers the perfect option.

articleTitle: A Modified Bottom Up Approach to Estimate Expected Demand Reduction During a Rare Event
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Smart Generation Computing, Communication and Networking (SMART GENCON)
abstract: Indian power system witnessed its largest very short-time demand ramping during light off event conducted to express solidarity with COVID-19 volunteers. 32 GW demand ramping was observed within 25 minutes and recorded as the highest ramping event across the globe. System operator has taken precautions and successfully handled the event with the help of hydro generation. However, system experienced severe frequency and voltage deviations due to unexpected consumer behaviour. A systematic study and an in-depth analysis of such a severe event would help system operators and planners to prepare for similar events. This paper presents a critical analysis of the activity and conducted a survey to understand consumer response during that event. It also proposes a modified Bottom-Up Approach to estimate Expected Demand Reduction (EDR) for such critical events. Proposed model is validated using data collected from the conducted survey. Proposed EDR estimation model offers better results than the Top Down and Bottom-up approach models used by system operator.

articleTitle: Automated Spam Detection Using Stochastic Gradient Descent with Self-Attentive Deep Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Smart Generation Computing, Communication and Networking (SMART GENCON)
abstract: Since the usage of the Internet is rising, individuals were connected virtually through social networking sites like Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, and so on. This has resulted in surge in the spread of unwanted messages called spam that is utilized for accumulating personal data, marketing, or to offend individuals. As a result, it becomes essential to have a stronger spam detection method that might thwart this type of message. Spam detection is the most important machine learning-oriented application over the past few years. Simultaneously, spam detection on noisy platforms like Twitter which remains a challenge because of high variability and short text in the language used on social networking platforms. To resolve these issues, this paper presents an automated spam detection using stochastic gradient descent with deep learning (ASD-SGDDL) technique. The presented method had a focus towards the detection of spam in the Twitter data. The proposed ASD-SGDDL model pre-processes the tweets in different ways such as filtering, tokenization, stop word removal, and n-gram construction. Followed by, the ASD-SGDDL model utilizes self-attentive deep learning (SADL) method for spam detection and classification. For improving the performance of detection in the presented method, the hyperparameter tuning process can be carried out by utilizing the SGD model. The experimental validation of the proposed method is examined on a benchmark dataset and the outcomes are examined interms of different measures. A wide ranging comparison study stated the enhanced performance of the ASD-SGDDL method to other existing models.

articleTitle: Above Average Below Achieving: The Role of Emphatic Digital Sanative Poetry Writing to Listen to Non-Regular Students' Silence
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Smart Generation Computing, Communication and Networking (SMART GENCON)
abstract: The obstacles students face during their final years of study may be caused by non-academic matters. This study attempts to specifically elaborate the roots of non-regular students' studying problems through their sanative poetry writing, choice of words, and metaphorical expressions. Sanative poetry writing application called Poe-Life utilizing emphatic technology is designed to provide an alternative creative writing tool. Data is gathered through each students” poem, its metaphorical textual analysis, questionnaires (DASS=Depression Anxiety Stress Scale and RSES=Rosenberg Self Esteem Scale), and deep interview with the students. The results show that students” learning difficulties stem from low self-esteem, higher anxiety regarding their learning and future pressures and fears of failure. The more favored poetic expressions are preferably done through digital poetry writing application than manual/traditional one, due to its practicality, emphatic modes and creative assistance through choices of hurting and healing words. The research implies that sanative poetry writing may be proposed as an alternative coaching medium to therapeutically assist non-regular students to better succeed their study.

articleTitle: A Review on Performance of Solar PV-Powered Battery and Diesel Generator Set Predicted EV Battery Swapping Charging Station
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Smart Generation Computing, Communication and Networking (SMART GENCON)
abstract: This paper presents the review and analysis of, an EV charging station powered by the grid (CS), a diesel generating set with an energy storage system, a solar PV (Photovoltaic) array, and battery are utilized. The charging station is primarily used to charge Battery storage using a BES and solar PV system. Smart utilization of the charging station can make use of a DG (Diesel Generator) unit or the grid to supply electricity in the event that the storage battery runs out or the solar array is unable to produce any. To maximize fuel efficiency, the DG sets are built to run at a constant 80–85 percent level of the model. High CO<inf>2</inf> emission from the transportation sector pollute the environment on a global scale. Adoption of electric vehicles (EV) offers a tremendous opportunity to reduce carbon emissions. Electric vehicles can be powered efficiently and more quickly at battery charging stations by using a battery swapping station (BSS) (BCS). The ideal solution is provided by Switching Technology for finishing a protracted statewide journey. The analysis of electric vehicle efficiency in many electrical elements is covered in this essay, along with the difficulties and benefits of using them as a logical step toward efficient, environmentally friendly, and sustainable transportation.

articleTitle: One Shot System Based Reliability Modelling And Analysis for Low-Cost Fault-Tolerant Computing System Comprising of One Instruction Cores
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Smart Generation Computing, Communication and Networking (SMART GENCON)
abstract: Rapid CMOS device size reduction resulted in billions of transistors on a chip have led to integration of many cores leading to many challenges such as increased power dissipation, thermal dissipation, occurrence of transient faults and permanent faults. In a multi-core scenario, the mitigation of transient faults and permanent faults at the core level using redundancy-based fault mitigation technique thereby improves the reliability of multi-core systems. In an asymmetric multi-core system, the smaller cores provide fault tolerance to larger cores is a core-level fault mitigation technique that has gained momentum and focus from a large number of researchers. The paper presents an economical, asymmetric multi-core system consisting of one instruction cores (MCS-OIC). The term “Low Cost” signifies power and area consumed by MCS-OIC. In MCS-OIC, MIPS cores are the conventional core and OICs are support standby redundant core. OICs pro-vide functional support to conventional cores for shorter periods of time. Failure in Arithmetic Logic Unit to execute instructions result in transfer of operation codes to OIC. OIC executes failed instructions by the repeated execution of one instruction named “subleq”. The behavior of OICs in MCS-OIC is modelled using a One-Shot System (OSS) model for reliability analysis. The OSS based reliability model allows effectively map the model parameters to core-level and functional-level probabilities to estimate the system reliability. Increase in number of OICs results in enhancement system reliability is validated using simulation results, thereby scalability of the MCS-OIC is observed.

articleTitle: Estimation of Direction-of-Arrival with Limited Snapshots in Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Smart Generation Computing, Communication and Networking (SMART GENCON)
abstract: The direction of arrival (DoA) estimation is an important problem in wireless sensor networks (WSNs) for source localization and tracking. Most of the algorithms in literature required more number of snapshots to get desired performance. But in an energy constrained sensor network, the data communication is to be less. Single snapshot based DOA estimation using comprehensive sensing is proposed in recent literature. But the performance is inconsistent, because of regularization parameters involved in the optimization process. The performance of complex correlation based DOA estimation with a single snapshot is good at a very high signal to noise ratio (SNR). Further, in WSN the first snapshot may be dominated by noise, then these methods will fail to provide desired results. Keeping these problems in mind, Frobinus norm based DOA estimation is proposed here. Even if the first snapshot failed we can extend for a few more snapshots to improve the performance. The simulation results show that the new method outperforms when the number of snapshots are increased to two or three compared to state-of-the art methods in literature.

articleTitle: IoT and Machine Learning-Based Systems for Predicting Cattle Health Status for Precision Livestock Farming
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Smart Generation Computing, Communication and Networking (SMART GENCON)
abstract: The livestock farming industry has turned into a focal point for research nowadays. Particularly, the animal health conditions are of utmost importance because the human beings are dependent on animals in order to fulfil their requirements of dairy products and meat. Instead of reacting to diseases after their outbreak, the modern technologies present a possibility for monitoring the key health parameters of animals on a regular basis such as amount of food and fluids consumed, movement, body condition score etc. By collecting this information and applying advanced artificial intelligence and machine learning, the farmers can recognize, foresee and avert the outbreak of animal diseases, which can aid them in better decision making and perform timely interventions. A review of the literature on the use of Internet of Things and machine learning based systems to predict the health status of cattle by measuring their health parameters using different types of sensors and other wearable technologies for precision livestock farming is presented in this study.

articleTitle: Design of a Q-learning based Smart Grid and smart Water scheduling model based on Heterogeneous Task Specific Offloading process
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Smart Generation Computing, Communication and Networking (SMART GENCON)
abstract: Smart cities require deployment & management of multiple Internet-of-Things (IoT) devices that can sense, communicate & perform information-specific actions. One of the most important tasks for deployment of these devices is controlling their scheduling operations. Existing smart city deployment models are either highly complex, or cannot be scaled beyond a certain set of devices, which limits their deployment capabilities. Moreover, most of these deployments are suited for a limited number of nodal traffic, which further affects their scalability levels. To overcome these issues, this text proposes design of a Q-learning based task scheduling Model that can uses Edge-Based Heterogeneous Task Specific Offloading (HTSO) with Genetic Algorithm (GA) based optimizations. The Q-learning model initially clusters tasks based on their importance-levels, which are determined by the number of real-time request types. High-capacity edge nodes and edge computing devices have their sleep patterns determined by these clusters depending on their relative importance levels. All of these choices are made by VMs in the edge devices, which helps to keep all of the edge computers in sync with one another. The Q-Learning Model may determine task-edge device mapping schedules based on priority levels of tasks and the computing efficiency of edge devices. Finding computationally-free edge devices using the GA Model, then assigning them duties depending on priority levels for those activities. Combining Q-Learning with GA allows the model to improve its computing efficiency for Smart Grid & Smart Water scheduling scenarios. This is accompanied with reduced average access latency, average response delay, and energy usage levels. The model was deployed on multiple smart city scenarios, and its performance was compared w.r.t. different standard deployment models. Based on this comparison, it was observed that the proposed model was able to improve scheduling efficiency by 15.5% for smart grids, and 8.3% for smart water scheduling, increase scheduling speed by 3.9% for smart grids, and 4.5% for smart water scheduling, while maintaining high computational efficiency of 99.5% for both the applications. Due to these advantages, the proposed model is capable of deployment for a wide variety of smart city use cases.

articleTitle: High Security Data Sharing on Edge Server by Smart IoT Users
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Smart Generation Computing, Communication and Networking (SMART GENCON)
abstract: With the meteoric rise of technology advancements, new needs have arrived. Internet happens to be one of those. The quest to make it more advanced and further the degree of convenience provided by it made way for Internet of Things (IOT) which is used for connecting the smart gadgets to the internet. To add more advantage to it one uses cloud with it where all the data produced is stored which reduces the burden of smart gadgets. Edge servers are used by deploying them close to the smart gadgets and can be used for communication and provide security operations. In this paper, an attempt is made to improve the time for searching in secure cloud on edge server. In the proposed results, the time duration is improved without compromising the security features. This gives better interface for the user to interact and share data with high security and search and download it through secure server in less processing time.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Different Models of Deep Learning for Prediction of Renal Cell Carcinoma
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Smart Generation Computing, Communication and Networking (SMART GENCON)
abstract: RCC (renal cell carcinoma) are one of the most common diseases that can be seen in an old age group today. For this problem, the technologists give the CT SCAN, MRI, and ultrasound images, so that the doctor or nephrologist can predict whether the disease is present or not. For this prediction problem, much research has been done on various approaches in the field of AI. Now researchers are making different models for better accuracy. In this paper, we have taken CT SCAN images from Radiopedia and then applied different models of deep learning for prediction. We compared each model for RCC prediction. We find that our model accuracy is 100%. We have also compared our model with other papers. We have concluded that many papers have used CNN because of huge image datasets and their models are failing when small datasets are applied.

articleTitle: Algorithmic Analysis on MGSR Optimization for Diagnosing Diabetic Retinopathy
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Smart Generation Computing, Communication and Networking (SMART GENCON)
abstract: The diabetes over long period of time leads to vision loss around the world. Although most of the studies related to DR provide an enhancement, still the scarcity in treatment and clinical practice patterns for diagnosis remains a major issue. The major concept of this paper is to propose the automatic detection of DR by investigating the retinal abnormalities such as, haemorrhages, soft exudates, hard exudates, and microaneurysm. The steps involved are the “pre-processing, optic disk removal, blood vessel removal, segmentation of abnormalities, feature extraction, optimal feature selection, and classification”. The preprocessing is performed by CLAHE and the optic disc removed is by a technique known as open-close watershed transformation. Grey Level thresholding segments and removes the blood vessels. Gabor filtering and Top hat transformation performs the segmentation of abnormalities. Feature extraction phase extracts the features such as, Texture Energy Measurement (TEM), Local Binary Pattern (LBP), Kapur's and Shanon's entropy. Feature selection process chooses the unique features containing minimum correlation. The images are classified into normal, earlier, moderate, or severe stages with the help of DBN based classification algorithm. The enhanced meta-heuristic algorithm known as “Modified Gear and Steering-based Rider Optimization Algorithm (MGS-ROA)” performs the optimal set of feature selection and the weight update in DBN. At last, the performance analysis is carried out by varying the time normalized value of MSG-ROA with respect to various performance measures.

Author Keywords: “Modified Gear and Steering-based Rider Optimization Algorithm”

articleTitle: An Explorative Analysis of IoT Security on Federated Intelligent Networks
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Smart Generation Computing, Communication and Networking (SMART GENCON)
abstract: This paper describes the use of deep learning techniques in order to analyze the data generated by IoT devices and determine whether the data was generated as a part of the normal operation of that device or was it generated by a malicious node. The malicious node could cause attacks like denial-of-service attack or a brute force attack to bypass the password authentication of the target device. Deep learning is suggested to be an effective way of providing security to the devices that participate in an IoT network. This paper describes federated learning techniques which are utilized since the IoT devices tend to have less processing power sufficient for the normal operation of the device while conserving the rest in order to minimize the cost. Certain vulnerabilities arise in the system due to the use of federated learning techniques namely lack of incentive to individual nodes and poisoning of the global model. We propose a blockchain based solution to provide incentive to the individual nodes in terms of credits. The incentive is in proportion to the amount of contribution provided by the given node. The resultant updates generated by compute nodes are verified based on the impact they will have on the global model before incorporating them into it.

articleTitle: Adaptive Distance Protection for Smart Grids with Infeed Compensation using Synchronized Phasor Measurements
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Smart Generation Computing, Communication and Networking (SMART GENCON)
abstract: Distance protection is one of the widely adopted schemes for the protection of transmission lines. This scheme provides a zone based protection and has inherent backup capabilities. But the scheme is prone to mal-operations under conditions where the network configurations is such that an infeed source is present within the reach of the relay. These infeeds affect the backup protection capability of distance relays. This paper shows the impact of infeed on existing distance protection scheme and proposes a new algorithm for distance relays that adaptively compensates for the effect of infeed using synchronized phasor measurements. The proposed work is specially designed for direct implementation in Smart Grid environment which has sophisticated communication infrastructure and advanced measuring devices such as the Phasor Measurement Units (PMUs). The newly proposed scheme is tested using simulation in MATLAB/Simulink. The relay algorithm is also implemented using Raspberry Pi microprocessor development kit with IOT based communication.

articleTitle: Monitoring Social Distancing using CNN for minimizing COVID-19
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Smart Generation Computing, Communication and Networking (SMART GENCON)
abstract: SARS-CoV-2 is the name of the highly infectious Coronavirus that brought the disease to the world. Preventing Covid by keeping the partition among people since it is not possible to get relatable information of an individual about its contamination. The WHO considers 6-ft to be a safe separation for individuals who take all other necessary precautions (masks, sanitizing, etc.)[1]. The undertaking targets utilizing Artificial Insight to implement this social separation openly put by continually checking the separation between individuals shown in a video feed, also alarming the dependable individual to initiate the required moves. This video feed can be used without any problem gathered by the prior framework across the general population places like CCTV Cameras. This would enable us to continually observe the separation between any two people in a public place. The adaptability is exceptionally arranged highly, so that cameras are introduced at practically on every open spots[2].

articleTitle: Performances of Popular Programming Languages for Towers of Hanoi Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Smart Generation Computing, Communication and Networking (SMART GENCON)
abstract: Looking at the growth of Popular Programming Languages(PPLs) like Python, Java and C++ in the fields of Artificial Intelligence, Data sciences and Machine learnings and other related concerns, and giving consideration to the recent research studies made in[11] [10] for nlogn and n<sup>2</sup> class of algorithms, in this study we have considered the Exponential (a very high time complex) Algorithm of Towers of Hanoi problem by implementing it using C++, Java and Python in-order to observe and measure the performances and verify the behaviors. The results of our experiments have found to be interesting and also verifies the previous published work referred above. Finally the performances of PPLs are described with respects to the results obtained. These results shall play a role to Bench mark in selection of popular programming languages for Domain specific Applications.

articleTitle: Comparison of Simulators based on Scenario-based Testing of Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Smart Generation Computing, Communication and Networking (SMART GENCON)
abstract: The future of modern transportation could be greatly improved by autonomous driving. However, its reliability and safety have drawn a lot of attention and concerns. This new paradigm poses unique challenges for testing. The expense and risk of testing an autonomous car algorithms on actual an autonomous vehicles are prohibitive. So many researchers cannot afford real AVs for testing on the roads. However, comprehensive and rigorous testing is crucial for ensuring that AVs can manage the wide range of conditions that can be seen on public roads. It is expensive and risky to test AVs on public roads. This is a challenge that is addressed by simulation testing, However, the disadvantage of simulation testing is that it is only as effective as the testing simulator and the degree to which the simulated situations faithfully represent the actual world. The fundamental characteristics that a successful simulator should have are outlined in this article. Further, we provide a comparison of commonly used simulators namely CARMAKER, CARLA, and LGSVL. Our analysis reveals that, for the reasons stated in this work, the Carmaker simulator is superior to the most cutting-edge simulators available now for testing self-driving cars end-to-end are CARLA and LGSVL. Analysis of simulator is based on Pedestrian scenario testing in different software. We demonstrate that by using this software, we can more efficiently test scenarios for an autonomous vehicles.

articleTitle: Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT): Testbed and Datasets for CyberSecurity and Digital Forensics
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Smart Generation Computing, Communication and Networking (SMART GENCON)
abstract: Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) datasets are hard to obtain due to confidentiality and security reasons. Consequently, evaluation of security solutions tailored for IIoT systems bears a significant research gap in the industrial security domain. An IIoT testbed that represents real-world scenarios comprising physical processes and its related controls would enable researchers to deploy and analyze solutions better, to explore and model vulnerabilities, understand the flow of data for forensic purposes, and to model viable datasets that help test and validate security measures. However, development and implementation of such testbeds is highly composite and brings along significant challenges upfront. In addition, the existence of legacy systems in the industrial environments, such as SCADA systems, hinders prompt deployment of sophisticated security controls against industrial systems. We propose the design of an IIoT testbed that comprises a wide range of physical processes through diverse controllers, applications, and devices interacting with each other and fostering acquisition of multidimensional data from diverse data sources. In addition, we propose a realistic IIoT dataset that would facilitate understanding of traffic flow and device/application analysis for our Digital Forensic Readiness (DFR) experimentation.

articleTitle: Sound Localisation of an Acoustic Source Using Time Delay and Distance Estimation
publicationTitle: 2022 International Conference on Smart Generation Computing, Communication and Networking (SMART GENCON)
abstract: Sound signals have been widely applied in various fields. One of the popular applications is sound localization, where the location and direction of a sound source are determined by analyzing the sound signal. For the past few decades, a wide variety of techniques have been proposed to find the position of source consisting active and passive localization. Autonomous vehicles use sound localization to predict the position of other vehicles and obstacles, and also in bad weather conditions. The main objective of this study is to localise the acoustic source using two microphones. The first step involved the calculation of time delay of two audio signals using cross-correlation, followed by determining the Direction of sound source in an Indoor Environment using TDOA and DOA algorithms as time delay estimation techniques. At the last step of the process, predicting the distance of the sound source using various machine learning algorithms was achieved. In this study, two microphones were used to locate the sound source in an indoor environment. The TDOA (Time Delay of Arrival) technique dealt with the problem of delay in the reception of sound signals from two microphone arrays by using the generalized cross-correlation algorithm to calculate the time delay. The time delay between the two audio signals was further used to calculate the angle at which the sound source was located. A machine learning model using Multivariate regression technique was developed that was trained on the recorded data to predict the distance of the sound source was also developed. The sound features such as rms energy, chroma STFT, spectral centroid, spectral bandwidth, spectral rolloff are given into the multivariate regression algorithm as the dependent variables and the distance of the source as independent variable which was the output parameter of the model. The proposed microphone system with the algorithm can successfully estimate the sound source's location. The sound localisation system can estimate the angle of arrival of the sound source signal with an error less than 8–10 degrees. The machine learning model predicted the distances in the range of 10 metres with an error of approximately 50-80cm while the error increased to 150-200cm when the distance was increased beyond 10 meters. The accuracy of multivariate regression was observed to be the highest (77%) among the machine learning models used in this project.
